newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--In an unaccustomed step for Greek prime ministers, Premier Costas Simitis yesterday visited the development ministry to be briefed by minister Vasso Papandreou on industry, trade, energy and technology issues. Simitis later criticised the private sector for not applying for EU funds, and subsequent low absorption rates.

--The other side of the coin fell at the Athens bourse yesterday: the general price index closed down (1.77 percent) for the first time in weeks. Sources say the development was expected and a normal development.
--Shop assistants and traders yesterday came to a compromise on trading hours. Stores will close at 8 pm on weekdays (9pm in summer) and 6 pm on Saturdays year-round. Opening hours are undefined.

--Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis and representatives of mutual fund management firms met at the ministry yesterday to examine the matter of issuing a cpi-indexed bond. The meeting discussed whether the bond should be modelled on the Swedish or US system.
IMERISIA

--Simitis yesterday extended an invitation to the business world to exploit EU funds, with 300 billion drachmas in the first half-year alone available for industrial investment in transport, telecoms and energy.
--Germany and other EU states are pushing for more flexible Maastricht criteria, creating favourable conditions for the speedier inclusion of the drachma in the Euro.

--A critical meeting on the future of OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, will be held today at the national economy ministry. The meeting is expected to decide on the procedures for OTE's second float.
--New legislation provides incentives for shipowners to build their vessels in Greece.
--The Technical Chamber has claimed that foreign construction companies are receiving favourable treatment from foreign consultants assigned to the Egnatia Highway project.
KERDOS

--The government's social dialogue is geared towards a national consensus to reduce inflation, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou says. "The reduction of inflation is not the sole responsibility of the government: it is the duty of all society," he says.
--A new tender for the sale of Cretabank is expected within the next ten days, sources say. The change in this tender will be the manner in which payment will be made.
EXPRESS

--The European Commission's latest annual report has corrected a previous mistake in the calculation of Greece's public deficit, and now says it is is no danger of having Cohesion Fund monies suspended.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Some 123 bilion drachmas have been secured for the construction of road works. Of that amount, 116.7 billion will go to the Egnatia Highway, and 6.3 billion to the Patras-Athens-Thessaloniki-Evzones (border) road axis.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
